Subject: Deployment mode & compliance requirements (HIPAA / SOC 2)

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand Elara's production requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap:
- Workload: claims adjudication + patient data enrichment (PHI) — strong reason for HIPAA protections and a signed BAA.
- Expected traffic: ~50 TPS peak, bursts to 150 TPS during overnight batch windows; low 99th latency requirement (~200ms per request for critical paths).
- Deployment modes under consideration: Private VPC/on-prem (preferred for data residency), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput + isolation), Hosted API (fastest to get started — but may need additional controls).
- Compliance asks: HIPAA/BAA, SOC 2 Type II evidence, audit log retention (7+ years), KMS/HSM support for encryption, and support for periodic penetration testing evidence.

Attachments I'm sharing in this thread: SOC2-report-2025.pdf (summary), BAA-draft-Redwood.docx (editable draft), network-arch-diagram.png (high-level).

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll loop in Marissa (Solutions Engineer) and Neha (Compliance lead) for a technical deep dive focused on network & key management — can we do Aug 12 at 11:00 AM PT?
2) Your security team to review the attached SOC2 summary + BAA draft; we'll provide the full SOC2 package under NDA if needed.
3) I'll follow up with region/residency options for Dedicated and Private deployment and the HSM/KMS integration details.

Let me know if Aug 12 works or suggest alternate times. Thanks,

--

Hi Alex / Priya — answering your two questions below and adding a couple of implementation notes ahead of the Aug 12 deep dive.

1) KMS / HSM:
- Private (VPC/on-prem) supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and HSM-backed key storage. We can also support CloudHSM via an approved network peering arrangement for Private deployments.
- Dedicated: integrates with cloud provider KMS (AWS KMS) for key wrapping and envelope encryption; if you need a customer-controlled HSM we can discuss options (customer-owned HSM + private connectivity).

2) Region / residency:
- Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in us-west-2 for committed pools (we have capacity partners in that region).
- Private VPC gives you the strongest residency assurance and network isolation if required by procurement/audit.

Notes:
- SOC2 evidence: attached is the 2025 SOC 2 summary. For full Type II artifacts we require an NDA; we can provide the SOC auditor contact for direct validation.
- BAA: attached draft is editable — we routinely iterate on customer redlines.
- Audit logs / retention: we support configurable retention windows up to 10 years for audit logs and can export logs to your SIEM.

I've attached the documents again here for convenience. Confirming Marissa will lead the tech deep dive on Aug 12 (11:00 AM PT). I'll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda: network diagram, KMS options, expected throughput test plan, and evidence handoff.

DocuSign link for BAA (optional sign now): https://app.docusign.com/BAA/ELARA-1247
Compliance docs: https://redwood.com/docs/compliance/hipaa-soc2

Thanks,
